hero.headline: Martin County moves to rewrite beach fishing rules after shark fishing complaints
hero.teaser: Martin County commissioners are rewriting the rules on fishing from public beaches after complaints that shark fishermen are using drones and remote-controlled boats to drop chum offshore and lure sharks closer to swimming areas.
hero.body:
Martin County commissioners told county staff Tuesday to draft a new ordinance that would restrict fishing from public beaches based on public safety concerns. County attorneys told commissioners that Florida law allows fishing from public beaches and takes precedence over conflicting county ordinances. The county banned fishing from public beaches years ago, but local fishermen have recently pushed back, arguing the rule amounts to government overreach.

Commissioners heard complaints that some fishermen are using drones or remote-controlled boats to carry bait offshore before dropping it into the water, potentially allowing them to skirt the state restriction on chumming directly from the beach. Under the proposal, fishing could be prohibited from county beaches during lifeguard hours, when swimmers are most likely to be in the water. The revised ordinance would also prohibit fishing from boat docks while boats are being launched or returning to shore.

One commissioner said the county's beaches are crown jewels on Hutchinson Island and must protect bathers, warning that people will go elsewhere if this kind of activity continues. Commissioners directed county staff to draft the new ordinance and bring it back for a future vote. Some residents argued the proposal does not go far enough, with one speaker saying the restrictions should extend to all Martin County beaches regardless of whether lifeguards are present.

cards.headline: Martin County School District adjusts bus routes to save $255,000
cards.teaser: The Martin County School District has approved changes to its bus routes for the upcoming school year, aiming to improve efficiency and reduce costs.
cards.body:
The new routes, which will begin on August 10, will consolidate existing routes while keeping bus stops and buses unchanged from last year. According to the district's director of transportation, the changes address a decline in ridership and will save the district the cost of operating three bus routes. Ruth, the district's director of transportation, said a route that only has two tiers might now pick up an extra tier, such as adding a middle school to a route that already serves elementary and high school, and drivers will get paid for what they work.

The district also cited a shortage of bus drivers as part of the reason for the decision. No jobs were lost as a result of the changes. Parents can track their child's bus route in real time using the MyReaxium app. The route changes also include activity buses for after-school programs. The school district said the changes will save $255,000.

cards.headline: Big Taste of Martin County fundraiser to support Big Brothers Big Sisters mentoring programs Oct. 6
cards.teaser: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will hold its Big Taste of Martin County fundraiser on Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart.
cards.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties is preparing for the return of Big Taste of Martin County, a food and spirits event scheduled for Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The annual fundraiser brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast.

 Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards and local bragging rights. The event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are currently waiting to be matched with a mentor, known as a Big. Spritz Stuart plans to feature several menu items during the event, including a Tuscan salmon dish, a smash burger and a specialty cocktail called the Fig & Flame.

 Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties serves children and families throughout Palm Beach and Martin counties through one-on-one mentoring relationships designed to support academic achievement, confidence and personal growth. Community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue warns station brownouts, higher insurance premiums possible under tax amendment
cards.teaser: Martin County Commissioner James Blake Capps said a no-overtime policy for fire rescue personnel could result in randomized brownouts of stations if the tax amendment passes.
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue projects it could lose 116 firefighters over the next two years about one third of its workforce because of reduced property tax revenue tied to a proposed constitutional amendment on the November ballot. County leaders warned the proposed cuts could lead to longer emergency response times and affect specialized emergency services provided throughout Martin County. Fire Rescue leaders discussed potential operational changes if those revenue reductions occur.

 Commissioner James Blake Capps said there would have to be a no-overtime policy for all fire rescue personnel. That doesn't sound so bad initially, but the consequences mean no backfilling of stations with personnel, which would result in randomized brownouts of stations. Capps also said if the county shuts down three fire stations, a lot of people would end up paying more for homeowner's insurance because they would be farther than five miles away from a fire station.

 County leaders have previously said the department has few options to absorb the projected revenue loss because about 93% of the Fire Rescue budget is dedicated to personnel. No vote on firefighter layoffs or fire station closures was expected during Tuesday's meeting. Voters will have the final say on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.

cards.headline: Martin County projects $16.5 million annual Fire Rescue budget loss under proposed homestead exemption
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue projects its annual budget would decline by $9.5 million in the first year if voters approve expanded homestead exemptions in November.
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue projects its annual budget would decline by $9.5 million in the first year under a proposed expansion of Florida's homestead exemption. By the second year, the annual loss would reach $16.5 million, a 22% reduction from the department's current budget. Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli presented the planning exercise during Tuesday's commission meeting.

 Under the scenario, Fire Rescue could close Station 18 on Britt Road, Station 33 in Hobe Sound, and Station 23 on Kanner Highway. The department could be forced to lay off as many as 116 firefighters by the second year, equivalent to one of the department's three shifts. The funding loss could force Martin County to eliminate specialized teams responsible for hazardous materials incidents, technical rescues and dive operations.

 Cianciulli pointed to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in Texas as an example of delays that can occur when a community must rely on outside resources. In an interview after the meeting, Cianciulli said they had to call for outside assets, a 14 hour response to start mitigating that scene. He said Martin County is in a position where if any incident happens, they are able to do an immediate mitigation without wasting any second.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Chief warns property tax reform could force closure of fire stations, cut 116 firefighters
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli warned commissioners Tuesday that proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts to fire and rescue operatio
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli warned commissioners Tuesday that proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts to fire and rescue operations in Martin County. The reform would expand homestead exemptions, potentially reducing the department's budget and forcing major reductions in service.

 Among the potential cuts outlined by the chief are closing firehouses, ending hazmat, dive, and technical rescue programs, grounding the department's critical care helicopter, and using firefighting tools past their operational lifetime. The department could be forced to cut as many as 116 firefighters over the next two years, about one-third of its workforce. County documents show about 93% of the Fire Rescue budget is dedicated to personnel.

 Residents who attended the commission meeting had mixed reactions. One resident said fire service is a valuable thing that matters more than other services. Another resident questioned why cutting personnel pay to make up the shortfall was not part of the options.

 Commissioner Edward Ciampi said the county would need to do belt tightening and slashing of budgets elsewhere. Commissioner Eileen Vargas said the county only has so many dollars to go around and needs to tighten up.

 No decisions were made Tuesday. The presentation was an opportunity to gather information so the county can plan accordingly ahead of the November vote. Commissioner James Blake Capps said shutting down three fire stations could lead to higher insurance premiums for residents living more than five miles from a fire station and could increase response times with serious consequences for residents. Voters will have the final say on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County breaks ground on $70 million K-8 school consolidating three Fort Pierce campuses
hero.body:
A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one facility. The new school will be built on land behind Dan McCarty Middle School and is expected to welcome between 1,500 and 1,800 students when it opens. It will consolidate Dan McCarty Middle, St. Lucie Elementary and Lawnwood Elementary into a single campus.

Superintendent Jon Prince said the project is moving forward on time, on budget, and on schedule. The new facility will feature state-of-the-art technology and serve the north part of St. Lucie County. The decision to consolidate comes as the existing schools show their age. All three were built in the 1950s and 1960s. Dan McCarty Middle Principal Latricia Stubbs-James said some of the things in the current building are antiquated.

The district is funding the $70 million project in part by selling the properties where the three older schools currently stand, offsetting the cost of maintaining aging buildings. Prince said the K-8 model is already proven across the district, which operates 11 other K-8 schools. Attendance is better, test scores are better and grades are better in the K-8s, Prince said.

Stubbs-James said the K-8 model offers unique benefits for younger students. Kindergarten students can see what it looks like to be an eighth grader at a new K-8, she said. The new Fort Pierce K-8 school is expected to be completed in August 2028.

cards.headline: Big Apple Pizza in Fort Pierce transforms patio into free reading room for children
cards.teaser: Big Apple Pizza owner Scott Van Duzer is expanding the restaurant's free book program by transforming its outdoor patio into a dedicated reading room where children can pick up a book any time they visit.
cards.body:
Big Apple Pizza owner Scott Van Duzer is expanding the Fort Pierce restaurant's free book program by transforming its outdoor patio into a dedicated reading room where children can pick up a book any time they visit. For years, Van Duzer has kept shelves of free books inside the restaurant, inviting children to take one home at no cost. Van Duzer said the restaurant has simply run out of space inside, prompting the decision to turn the outdoor patio into a permanent reading room.

Van Duzer said giving back has always been part of the restaurant's mission. He said that commitment comes from the example his mother set while he was growing up. My mom was pretty instrumental in my life so she just said if you can give back, give back. We live that every day, Van Duzer said.

Construction on the new reading room is underway and is expected to be completed later this fall. Until then, children can continue picking up free books inside Big Apple Pizza, where the message remains the same: every child is welcome to take a book home, no questions asked. Big Apple Pizza is located at 2311 S 35th St, Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police seek two suspects in ATM robbery on U.S. 1
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce Police are looking for two suspects who allegedly robbed a man of money outside a Wells Fargo in the 2500 block of South U.S. 1 on July 26.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce Police are looking for two men who allegedly robbed a man of an unknown amount of money outside the Wells Fargo in the 2500 block of South U.S. 1, Fort Pierce on July 26. At about 8:38 p.m., a man was approached by two men after the man used the ATM at the bank. The victim told police that the two men demanded money from him and that one of the men showed a handgun tucked in his waistband.

The two men forced the victim to withdraw money from the ATM and then fled on foot. Officers established a perimeter, deployed a K-9 and drone to search, but the suspects were not located. The suspects are described as two Hispanic males in their early 20s, approximately 5-foot, 10-inches tall and 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt, the victim told police. Anyone with information on the suspects is asked to call Fort Pierce Police at 772-467-6700.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents oppose proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe
cards.teaser: Residents and history advocates in Fort Pierce are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fearing the development could displace the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum.
cards.body:
Residents and history advocates in Fort Pierce are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fearing the development could displace the area's cultural heritage and the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum. The Port of Fort Pierce master plan draft for 2026 calls for replacing the existing area at Museum Pointe with large floating docks designed for mega yachts, along with a clubhouse, an event center and a water taxi connecting to Harbour Pointe to the north. The plan also proposes relocating the history museum.

Terry Howard, a passionate advocate for St. Lucie County's history, expressed disbelief over the proposed changes. This is a gem for the area, and I just can't believe they want to put mega yachts here, he said. The museum, it's our culture. It's the center for our culture for this county. Howard has started a petition opposing the proposed marina, hoping to raise awareness and preserve the location and its natural surroundings.

In a statement, St. Lucie County said that no plans have been approved and feedback from the board will dictate future changes, modifications and clarifications to the draft document. The draft of the master plan is expected to go before the county commission in August.

cards.headline: 9-year-old killed, 12-year-old injured after dirt bike collision on Midway Road in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: A 9-year-old was killed, and a 12-year-old was injured Monday afternoon after a dirt bike collided with a FedEx truck on Midway Road in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
A 9-year-old was killed, and a 12-year-old was injured Monday afternoon after a dirt bike collided with a FedEx truck on Midway Road in St. Lucie County. The injured child has since been released from the hospital. Investigators say the two children were riding a dirt bike when they collided with a FedEx truck. The 9-year-old was killed. The 12-year-old was hurt and is now at home recovering.

Steven Baker, the attorney for the family of the injured 12-year-old, described the injuries the child sustained. He has a few broken bones and a tooth that's fractured, Baker said. Baker says the child is progressing physically but is also recovering mentally from the trauma of the crash. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office says since 2020, there have been 110 bike crashes in St. Lucie County, 15 of them involving children. On Midway Road specifically, there have been six reported crashes, two of which have involved children.

cards.headline: Three arrested in St. Lucie County after 3-month-old dies from severe dehydration and malnutrition
cards.teaser: Detectives with the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office have arrested three people in connection with the death of a 3-month-old infant in Fort Pierce, describing the case as one of the worst they have encountered.
cards.body:
Detectives with the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office have arrested three people in connection with the death of a 3-month-old infant, describing the case as one of the worst they have encountered. The investigation began in August of last year when detectives were called to a Fort Pierce home following the infant's death. The baby had been living with his grandfather, Robert Maxwell, and Robert Maxwell's girlfriend, Vikki Koon, while his mother, Nicole Maxwell, resided with a boyfriend in Vero Beach.

An autopsy revealed the infant was emaciated and had a sunken abdomen and widespread lesions consistent with severe dehydration and malnutrition. According to an arrest affidavit, Koon told deputies she believed a newborn should have two ounces per feeding twice a day. She said when she ran out of formula, she would fill the bottle with regular milk and add water. Investigators found the mobile home in poor condition. The house was extremely hot. There was a bug infestation in the home, lack of food in the home and the home was unsafe for walking, Detective Corporal Jennifer Diaz said.

All three suspects are facing several charges, including aggravated manslaughter. St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said protecting children is a responsibility we all share. If you see signs that a child may be neglected, abused, or living in unsafe conditions, do not assume someone else will intervene. One phone call can be the difference between a child receiving the help they need and a life being saved, Del Toro said.

cards.headline: Man accused of DUI after crashing SUV into Port St. Lucie liquor store
cards.teaser: Jimy Alvarenga Ramirez crashed the front of his SUV into 3rd Base Liquors before fleeing the scene on foot, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.
cards.body:
A man allegedly had one too many after authorities said he crashed into a liquor store Friday night. According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, Jimy Alvarenga Ramirez crashed the front of his SUV into 3rd Base Liquors before fleeing the scene on foot.

After the crash, witnesses provided a description of the driver, allowing officers to review surveillance footage and locate Alvarenga Ramirez several blocks away, where police said he was attempting to hide. No one was injured in the crash. Alvarenga Ramirez was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Museum of Art hosts free friendship bracelet workshop with recycled fishing line
hero.teaser: The Vero Beach Museum of Art will host a free Second Saturday program on Aug. 8 featuring hands-on activities that transform discarded fishing line into friendship bracelets. The p
hero.body:
The Vero Beach Museum of Art will host a free Second Saturday program on Aug. 8 featuring hands-on activities that transform discarded fishing line into friendship bracelets. The program runs from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. and includes docent-led gallery tours, studio art projects and lessons about protecting local marine life.

 Coastal Connections will lead the fishing line bracelet activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium. Participants can learn about the organization's Fishing Line Recycling Program while creating bracelets from line collected from local waterways. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

 The Nature in Layers art activity for children connects to the museum's current exhibitions through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can tour James Prosek: At Work in the Holmes Gallery and Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases in the Schumann and Titelman galleries throughout the day.

 Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership demonstrates how the organization works with the community to introduce marine conservation and environmental protection. The museum offers free admission throughout the day on Second Saturdays. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing sea turtle survival by educating and connecting people to the environment.

cards.headline: Three arrested in Fort Pierce after 3-month-old dies from dehydration, malnutrition
cards.teaser: Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce in Augus
cards.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce in August 2025. Nicole Maxwell, the child's mother, Robert Maxwell, the child's grandfather, and Vikki Koon, the grandfather's girlfriend, were arrested last week following a nearly year-long investigation by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

 The investigation began on Aug. 20, 2025, when deputies responded to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital after Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the infant to the emergency room. The child was pronounced dead on arrival. A medical examiner later determined the baby died from dehydration and malnutrition and ruled the death a homicide. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach, and the child exhibited lesions consistent with severe dehydration.

 The infant lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon at a mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce, while Nicole Maxwell lived with a boyfriend in Vero Beach. St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Detective Jennifer Diaz described the mobile home as having windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring, and live and dead cockroaches throughout.

 The home was extremely hot, with a bug infestation, lack of food, and unsafe conditions for walking, Diaz said. Koon told investigators she fed the infant only twice a day and when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in.

 Four other children of Nicole Maxwell who were living in the home, ranging in age from 2 to 10 years old, have been placed in foster care through the state Department of Children and Families. Robert Maxwell and Koon are held at the St. Lucie County Jail, each on $1.5 million bond. Nicole Maxwell was arrested July 23 at a home in the 300 block of 12th Street, SW, Vero Beach, and is held at the Indian River County Jail on no bond. A neighbor named Suzan said she witnessed the children asking for water and food, describing the conditions as unlivable.

cards.headline: Indian River County Fire Rescue visits Dodgertown Elementary for career fair
cards.teaser: Firefighters from Indian River County Fire Rescue spent time with students at Dodgertown Elementary on Tuesday, sharing what it is like to serve the community.
cards.body:
Indian River County Fire Rescue participated in a career fair at Dodgertown Elementary at 4350 43rd Street in Vero Beach on Tuesday, July 28. Firefighters spent time with students at the school, discussing what it is like to serve the community and introducing them to the various career opportunities available in the fire service.

 The event gave students a chance to ask questions and see the equipment firefighters use in their daily work. Indian River County Fire Rescue posted about the visit on Facebook, describing it as a day filled with learning and inspiration. "From answering great questions to showing off our equipment, it was a fantastic day of learning and inspiration," the department said in the statement.

 Fire Rescue officials said they hope the career fair will help inspire the next generation of firefighters, paramedics and public servants. The department emphasized the rewarding nature of careers in fire service during their time with the students. The firefighters shared information about serving the community and the different roles available within the department.

 The career fair represented an opportunity for young students to learn about public service careers firsthand from the firefighters who perform those jobs every day. By bringing equipment to the school and taking time to answer student questions, Fire Rescue aimed to give children a better understanding of what firefighters and paramedics do to help their community.

cards.headline: Cyclist rides through Vero Beach on 2,600-mile journey from Key West to Maine
cards.teaser: A Boston cyclist rode through Vero Beach this week on a 2,600-mile bike ride from Key West to Maine to honor a friend lost to colorectal cancer.
cards.body:
Jay Weedall traveled to South Florida to begin the journey, with a goal of raising $50,000 for the Young Onset Colorectal Cancer Research Center. Weedall began his journey in Key West, pedaling 155 miles to Miami on day one. He set off on his second leg, a 163-mile ride to Vero Beach, after filling his hydration pack with ice to stay cool.

 Weedall is riding roughly 150 miles a day up the coast through nearly every state all the way to the Pan Mass Challenge. He will do the Pan Mass Challenge across Massachusetts on August 2 and continue to the Canadian border in Maine. By avoiding highways, Weedall says the route offers something unexpected, allowing him to experience little coastal towns along the inlets. Fans can follow Weedall's journey on the cycling app Strava.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Police Department honors service of Indian River County firefighter
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands with Indian River County Fire Rescue following the death of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning the loss of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang, who passed away while off duty. The department said its thoughts are with his family, loved ones and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time and that it honors his service and the impact he made on the community.

 Indian River County Fire Rescue announced Lang's death Saturday night and thanked neighboring agencies that quickly shared messages of support following the announcement. The Sebastian Police Department said it stands alongside its brothers and sisters of Indian River County Fire Rescue as they mourn the heartbreaking loss and that Lang's dedication, courage and commitment to serving others will never be forgotten.

cards.headline: Sebastian Police, Vero Beach Police honor Indian River County firefighter Geoffrey Lang
cards.teaser: Multiple law enforcement agencies across Indian River County expressed condolences following the death of Firefighter/Paramedic Geoffrey Lang.
cards.body:
The Sebastian Police Department said it was standing alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning Lang's death. "Your bravery and service will always be remembered," the department wrote. The Vero Beach Police Department also shared its condolences, saying it stands alongside IRCFR during the difficult time.

 "Our thoughts are with his family, loved ones, and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time," the Vero Beach Police Department said. "We honor his service and the impact he made on our community." Indian River County Fire Rescue posted a photo on its Facebook page Saturday night acknowledging the end of watch for Lang.

 The Indian River County Sheriff's Office also expressed condolences. Anna Kirkland, Indian River Mosquito Control District Seat 2, said she was praying for Lang's family, friends, and the entire Indian River County Fire Rescue family. She thanked Lang for his service to the community.

cards.headline: Indian River County leaders remember firefighter Geoffrey Lang who worked out of Sebastian station
cards.teaser: Geoffrey Lang died on Saturday following a personal tragedy at his home in Sebastian, county spokeswoman Kathy Copeland said.
cards.body:
Lang, 35, was survived by his wife, two children and parents. Lang joined Indian River County Fire Rescue in 2015 and worked out of Station 9 at 13550 Roseland Road in Sebastian. Copeland said that Lang dedicated his career to serving the residents of Indian River County with professionalism and compassion. He was a valued member of the department, respected by his fellow firefighters, and known for his unwavering commitment to others.

 Indian River County Administrator John A. said that during this incredibly difficult time, the county's hearts go out to his family, friends and all who had the privilege of serving alongside him. Indian River County Fire Rescue Chief David Johnson said the department mourns the loss of one of its own and that Lang faithfully served the community for more than a decade.

 Indian River County Commission Chair Deryl Loar said Lang was a dedicated employee and the Board of County Commissioners and County Administration extends condolences to his family, friends and colleagues. All commissioners stand with Indian River Fire Rescue and remain committed to supporting the health and well-being of personnel including the importance of mental health support for first responders and their families.
